Ali registered for the draft on his eighteenth birthday and was drafted to serve in the Vietnam War. Appearing for his scheduled induction into the U.S. Armed Forces on April 28, 1967 in Houston, Ali refused three times to step forward at the call of his name and claimed the status of a Conscientious Objector due to his religious beliefs. An officer warned him he was committing a felony punishable by five years in prison and a fine of $10,000. Once more, Ali refused to budge when his name was called. As a result, he was arrested. On the same day the New York State Athletic Commission suspended his boxing license and stripped him of his title as heavyweight champion. Other boxing commissions followed suit. Ali would not be able to obtain a license to box in any state for over three years. At the trial on June 20, 1967, after only 21 minutes of deliberation, the jury found Ali guilty. After a Court of Appeals upheld the conviction, the case went to the U.S. Supreme Court. On June 28, 1971, the Supreme Court overturned Ali's conviction by a unanimous 8-0 decision (Justice Thurgood Marshall did not participate).

On June 4, 1967 Ali met in Cleveland to be questioned by other athletes and members of the Black American community to see just how strong Ali stood behind his convictions as a conscientious objector to the Vietnam War. Many of them had military backgrounds. Many attended to try to convince Ali to serve. Ali's answers would determine whether the group would support his stance, It was the convergence of key moments in both the the civil rights movement and the protest against the Vietnam War.

Following the meeting, Brown led the group to this press conference where he said the group supported Ali and his rights as a conscientious objector as they felt he was sincere in his belief.

Front Row L to R: Bill Russell of the Boston Celtics, Ali, Jim Brown of the Cleveland Browns, Lew Alcindor (later Kareem Abdul Jabar) of UCLA. Back Row: US Rep Stokes and former Cleveland mayor Stokes and various pro athletes including Bobby Mitchell (Washington Redskins), Sid Williams (Browns), Jim Shorter (Redskins), Walter Beach (Browns), John Wooten (Browns), Curtis McClinton (Kansas City Chiefs).
